chapter: Early bands and Luis Russell's Harlem
title: Turned away from the white Boy Scout troop
summary: Near the Dudley School he was frozen out of the white troop's meeting, his first outright experience of segregation.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I had ways of, I guess, of maneuvering. I remember – even in Boston – I was in the Boy Scouts, like I said earlier. They had – I was Troop Six. That was the Shaw House. It was black. One time, the Norfolk House was near me. It was probably as close to me as the Shaws. The Norfolk House was white. That was near where I went to school, almost across the street from the Dudley School. So one time I’m going to go put on my uniform and go up and check out their Scout. I forget what their troop number was. I went up there, and it was practically – I knew it. I said, “Okay, what’s up?” They said,
“No . . .” – they froze there. I was still at the same school across the street, but I couldn’t go to their scout meeting.
So that’s really your first experience with segregation?
That’s my first experience outright that I could really check out, see about that. They don’t want me here.
